items.title: Exact Dirac particle/antiparticle free model
items.statement:
Fix the oriented, time-oriented affine Minkowski spacetime and inertial length coordinates of [[def-qft-framework-units]], with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and $x^0=ct$. The parameter $\mu\ge0$ and wave vector $\mathbf k$ have unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$; $\omega(\mathbf k)=\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+\mu^2}$ also has unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$. For $\mu>0$, $\mu=m_{\mathrm{rest,SI}}c/\hbar$; $\mu=0$ is the admitted massless branch. The corresponding SI energy and momentum are $\hbar c\omega$ joules and $\hbar\mathbf k$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$. The canonically normalized Dirac field has engineering length degree $-3/2$; a spacetime spinor test has degree $-5/2$, making its spacetime-smearing pairing dimensionless. These are the unit conventions of [[def-qft-framework-units]], not claims about interacting-field scaling.

Adopt the Dirac branch of [[post-qft-free-field-model]]: one free Dirac species, the selected CAR representation and zero-particle vacuum are physical model assumptions. Countable Choice is the mathematical choice strength used by the Fock construction [[def-countable-choice]].

Use $\mathbb C^4$ spinors and the matrices, mass-shell parameter, one-particle Hilbert space $\mathcal H_D$, multiplier $h_D(\mathbf k)=\boldsymbol\alpha\cdot\mathbf k+\beta\mu$, projections $P_\pm(\mathbf k)$ and propagator $W_D$ defined in [[def-qft-dirac-projections]]. The mathematical supplier [[lem-qft-dirac-projection-matrices]] establishes that $P_\pm$ are complementary orthogonal projections of rank two, that $\mathcal H_\pm=\operatorname{ran}P_\pm$ are closed, and that $h_D$ is self-adjoint on its maximal multiplication domain. The one-particle space of the adopted field is
$$\mathcal K_D=\mathcal H_+\oplus\overline{\mathcal H_-},$$
where the bar denotes the conjugate Hilbert space. Its fermionic Fock space, vacuum and creation/annihilation maps use [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]] and [[lem-qft-fock-ccr-car]].

For a Schwartz spinor test $F\in\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb C^4)$, set
$$\widehat F(t,\mathbf k)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x}F(t,\mathbf x)\,d^3\mathbf x,\qquad u_F(\mathbf k)=\int_{\mathbb R}W_D(t,\mathbf k)\widehat F(t,\mathbf k)\,dt.$$
The physical field is the bounded smeared map
$$\Psi(F)=c(P_+u_F)+c^\dagger(\overline{P_-u_F}),$$
with the exact test-map and CAR construction of [[lem-qft-free-dirac-car-locality]]. It is antilinear in $F$. Its positive-energy branch is the particle annihilation term; the conjugate negative-energy branch occurs as antiparticle creation. This is a model assignment: it does not identify negative-energy Fock excitations with physical states, invoke a filled Dirac sea, or prove the general spin-statistics theorem. No pointwise field operator is defined here.

items.title: Dirac CAR, covariance, graded locality and positive Fock energy
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the adopted Dirac branch of [[post-qft-free-field-model]] as specified by [[def-qft-free-dirac-model]]. For all Schwartz spinor tests $F,G$, the bounded smeared field $\Psi$ is antilinear in its test, satisfies
$$\{\Psi(F),\Psi(G)\}=0,\qquad \{\Psi(F),\Psi(G)^\dagger\}=\langle u_F,u_G\rangle I,$$
and solves the tested free Dirac equation. If $F$ and $G$ have compact spacelike-separated supports, the field-field and field-adjoint anticommutators vanish; consequently, finite even polynomials in the bounded smeared fields commute across spacelike-separated regions.

Let $\widetilde G_D$ be the translation and explicit spin-lift group defined in [[lem-qft-dirac-covariance-spectrum]]. Its strongly continuous unitary Fock representation $U$ satisfies
$$U(\widetilde g)\Psi(F)U(\widetilde g)^{-1}=\Psi(\tau_{\widetilde g}F),\qquad \tau_{\widetilde g}F(x)=(S^{-1})^\dagger F(\Lambda^{-1}(x-a)),$$
for $\widetilde g=(a,\Lambda,S)$. For the explicit spatial rotation lift, $S_R(2\pi)=-I_4$ and $S_R(4\pi)=I_4$; hence the $2\pi$ test pullback is $F\mapsto-F$ and $U_{2\pi}\Psi(F)U_{2\pi}^{-1}=-\Psi(F)$, while the $4\pi$ test pullback and field action are identities. The vacuum is invariant and cyclic for the global graded field algebra. On the $n$-particle sector, $U_{2\pi}=(-1)^n I$ and $U_{4\pi}=I$.

The joint spectrum of translations lies in the closed future cone. If $K_D$ denotes the length-coordinate time-translation generator of [[lem-qft-dirac-covariance-spectrum]], its zero-energy eigenspace is $\ker K_D=\mathbb C\Omega$, where $\Omega$ is the normalized vacuum; thus normalized zero-energy vectors differ from $\Omega$ only by a complex phase. For $\mu>0$, the nonvacuum spectrum has gap at least $\mu$ in inverse-length units, hence $m_{\mathrm{rest,SI}}c^2$ in SI energy units. The physical energy is $H_D^{\mathrm{SI}}=\hbar cK_D\ge0$ on the same domain and has the same kernel. This Fock generator acts on a different Hilbert space from the first-quantized multiplier $h_D$, which has both signs of energy. These are conditional deductions in the adopted model, not empirical claims.

title: Exact Dirac particle/antiparticle free model — Examples

items.title: Two-pi spin rotation and even-observable invariance
items.statement: Define $\mathcal A_D^{\mathrm{even}}$ as the norm closure of finite linear combinations of the identity and even-degree products of $\Psi(F)$ and $\Psi(F)^\dagger$, for Schwartz spinor tests $F$. In the selected free Dirac model, let $U_{2\pi}$ implement a spatial rotation by $2\pi$ and let $U_{4\pi}$ implement a rotation by $4\pi$. On the $n$-particle sector of the adopted antisymmetric Fock decomposition, indexed by $n\in\mathbb N_0=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$, $U_{2\pi}$ acts as $(-1)^n$ times the identity; $U_{4\pi}=I$. Every finite even polynomial in bounded spacetime-smeared Dirac fields and their adjoints is invariant under conjugation by $U_{2\pi}$, and therefore so is $\mathcal A_D^{\mathrm{even}}$. This is an exact model calculation; it does not infer a general spin-statistics theorem.
